evaluator.name: README.en.md
evaluator.text:
# MLS-Bench

[中文](README.md) | English

The machine-readable facts are in [`MANIFEST.yaml`](MANIFEST.yaml); this page says what a reader needs and points to where each fact sits in the manifest.

## What it is

MLS-Bench (machine learning science) measures whether an agent can propose a new component, loss, optimizer or training procedure whose gain transfers across settings, seeds, datasets and scales: each task fixes a research scaffold (a real library such as scikit-learn),
gives the relevant source and strong baselines, and asks for one algorithmic change inside a constrained edit surface, judged over several settings and seeds and normalised against the baselines. There are 140 tasks in 12 ML research domains; this project uses only
the **22 tasks that need only a CPU and no external LLM API** (causal discovery, treatment effects, calibration, subgroup calibration shift, active learning, imputation, anomaly detection, clustering, dimensionality reduction, ensembles, symbolic regression, HPO, evolution strategies,
multi-objective optimisation, NAS, online bandits and so on) (source: MANIFEST.yaml `subset`, `item_info`).

- Paper: arXiv 2605.08678.
- Code and tasks: `Imbernoulli/MLS-Bench`, pinned commit `b873944969c53b01e4ee6e843c77767b8c702485`; **the repository has no licence file**. The Harbor bundle `harbor/tasks-docker/mls-bench__<task>/` of the repository is used.
- Task dataset: HF `Bohan22/MLS-Bench-Tasks` (MIT, revision `b50fe197b609b1225ba296dbacd0dd1a45fb4cf4`), the same content as the task definitions; this project only records its licence.
- Entry in this repository: asset id `mlsbench-repo` (the repository checkout, deletable and rebuildable), read through the link `assets/mlsbench-repo`; the tasks' base images `bohanlyu2022/mlsbench-harbor-<package>:latest` are pinned here **by digest**
  (manifest `run.base_images`, 2026-11-01), 0.2 to 7.8 GB compressed.

## Licence

The task dataset says MIT; the code repository has no licence; the third-party libraries and datasets the tasks use keep their own terms, and the base images on Docker Hub state no licence. This project did not check each one; it pulls the images and reads the task bundle for research evaluation only and never commits or redistributes them
(source: MANIFEST.yaml `license`).

## Items and batches

The 22 tasks are the manifest's `items` (the item name is the task name), e.g. `mlsbench/ml-anomaly-detection`. `uv run researchworld_eval tasks --benchmark mlsbench` lists them.
24 of the 140 tasks have `gpus = 0`; without `agent-tool-reasoning` and `mas-topology`, which call an external LLM API, 22 remain.

**There is no formal batch**: it is a training environment of the phase 3 experiment role (#141, #157); #157 chooses the items. `src/tasks/batches/mlsbench.yaml` is the whole set and is not in `plan.batches`.
Resources: 8 CPUs and 32 GB per task (64 GB for `ml-active-learning`); the official agent limit is 5 hours; verification runs in the same task container and takes from tens of seconds to hours.

## How it runs and is scored

- Official entry: the Harbor bundle lets any Harbor agent work in the task environment (`harbor run -c run.yaml --path tasks-docker/mls-bench__<task> --agent <agent>`); scoring is Harbor's verifier `tests/test.sh`, with no LLM (source: MANIFEST.yaml `run`).
- The verifier: an edit-range guard (against `tests/meta/pristine`; a change outside the editable ranges or a new file is invalid and the reward is 0) → every eval script of the task (hidden settings included) → the metrics are parsed and normalised against the baselines by the `score_spec` into `combined_score`, clipped to [0, 1] and written as `reward.txt`.

## One item: what the system gets and how it is scored (Issue #161)

Written `mlsbench/<task>`; coding-agent and ResearchWorld can run it:

```bash
uv run researchworld_eval run coding-agent mlsbench/ml-anomaly-detection --condition CC-sonnet --purpose smoke
uv run researchworld_eval score mlsbench-verifier <run-id>
```

- **Given (candidate side, rendered by `researchworld_eval.benchmarks.mlsbench`)**: the task's environment image (`rwe-bench-mls-env:<task>-<hash>`, the base image pinned by digest, the scaffold at `/workspace`); the prompt is `instruction.md` verbatim;
  a system that can work inside the image (coding-agent, ResearchWorld) does, any other system gets `/workspace` copied out of the image (aliased at `/workspace`).
- **Not given**: `tests/` (eval scripts, hidden settings, parser, score spec, the baseline leaderboard, the pristine tree) and `solution/` (the oracle); Harbor mounts them only at verification. The framework refuses a candidate side that holds a file with one of these names.
- **Deliverables**: the editable files the task declares (`files[].filename` of `tests/meta/config.json`, e.g. `/workspace/scikit-learn/custom_anomaly.py`).
- **Time limit**: the official 5 hours (`task.toml`), with the CPUs and memory, as the item's conditions; within the framework-wide one-week cap.
- **Network shield**: `task.toml` says `allow_internet = true`, but the base image carries the data, so it runs as an offline item with only the package index allowed (common problem C4). The shield ([`shield.yaml`](shield.yaml)) blocks the benchmark's own material:
  the repository, the task dataset, the paper, the leaderboard site and the task images on Docker Hub; MLS-Bench tasks are not derived from a single paper, so there is no per-item original paper; the date cap is the repository's creation date 2026-05-08.
- **Scoring**: the evaluator [`mlsbench-verifier`](../../../evaluators/mlsbench_verifier/README.en.md), headline `metrics.reward` (0-1).

### Differences from the official protocol

- Officially Harbor verifies the whole `/workspace` after the agent; here only the delivered editable files are uploaded to the verifier. A change outside the ranges or a new file is not seen by the guard (more lenient than official); changes inside the ranges are scored as officially.
- The base image is pinned by digest, not `latest`.
- Only the package index is reachable.
- This machine runs Harbor 0.20.0 (the authors tested 0.6.6 and 0.22.0); the `schema_version = "1.1"` bundle parses and runs on 0.20.0 (shown by the smoke runs).

## Published reference scores

Read 2026-11-01 from the [leaderboard](https://mls-bench.com/leaderboard) page's embedded data: the MLS-Bench Lite (30 tasks) total, human SOTA 44.66:

| model | configuration | total |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Fable 5.1 | Claude Code (max effort) | 50.3 |
| GPT-6 Astra | Codex (max) | 50.0 |
| Claude Opus 5 | Claude Code (max effort) | 49.8 |
| Kimi K3 | Kimi-Code (max) | 48.3 |
| GPT 5.6 Sol | Codex (max) | 46.2 |
| Qwen3.8-Max | Claude Code | 41.0 |
| Claude Sonnet 5 | Claude Code (max effort) | 31.4 |

(Source: MANIFEST.yaml `published_scores`. The leaderboard has only the 30-task Lite total, most of whose tasks need a GPU; there are no per-task scores and no separate total for the 22 CPU tasks, so nothing is registered as a #127 per-task baseline.)

## Smoke (Issue #161)

The same task `mlsbench/ml-anomaly-detection` (unsupervised tabular anomaly detection, scikit-learn base image, 4 evaluation settings), once per system, `--purpose smoke`, **time limit 1 hour** (officially 5 hours; the smoke only shows that the integration runs through, so the budget was cut with `--hours 1`), scored by `mlsbench-verifier` (Harbor 0.20.0, no LLM):

# MLS-Bench

中文 | [English](README.en.md)

机器可读的事实在 [`MANIFEST.yaml`](MANIFEST.yaml)；本文只说明读者需要知道的内容，并指出每条事实在 manifest 里的位置。

## 是什么

MLS-Bench（machine learning science）衡量 agent 能不能提出一个新的组件、损失、优化器或训练流程，并且收益能迁移到不同设置、种子、数据集和规模上：每题固定一个研究 scaffold（真实的库，如 scikit-learn），
给出相关源码和强基线，要求在受限的可编辑区里做一处算法改动，跨多个设置和种子评测，按基线归一化。共 140 题、12 个 ML 研究领域；本项目只接其中 **22 个只用 CPU、不调外部 LLM API 的题**
（因果发现、处理效应、校准、子群校准漂移、主动学习、插补、异常检测、聚类、降维、集成、符号回归、HPO、进化策略、多目标优化、NAS、在线 bandit 等）（来源：MANIFEST.yaml `subset`、`item_info`）。

- 论文：arXiv 2605.08678。
- 代码和任务：`Imbernoulli/MLS-Bench`，固定 commit `b873944969c53b01e4ee6e843c77767b8c702485`；**仓库没有许可证文件**。用的是仓库里的 Harbor 包 `harbor/tasks-docker/mls-bench__<任务>/`。
- 任务数据集：HF `Bohan22/MLS-Bench-Tasks`（MIT，revision `b50fe197b609b1225ba296dbacd0dd1a45fb4cf4`），与任务定义同内容；本项目只登记它的许可。
- 本仓库的入口：资产 id `mlsbench-repo`（仓库检出，可删除后重建），经 `assets/mlsbench-repo` 链接读取；任务的基础镜像 `bohanlyu2022/mlsbench-harbor-<包>:latest` 本项目按 **digest** 固定（manifest `run.base_images`，2026-11-01），
  压缩后 0.2–7.8 GB 不等。

## 许可

任务数据集标 MIT；代码仓库没有许可证；任务用到的第三方库和数据集沿用各自条款，Docker Hub 上的基础镜像没有许可说明。本项目没有逐个核对，只拉取镜像、读取任务包用于研究评测，不提交、不再分发（来源：MANIFEST.yaml `license`）。

## 题目和批次

22 题的名单是 manifest 的 `items`（题号就是任务名），例如 `mlsbench/ml-anomaly-detection`。`uv run researchworld_eval tasks --benchmark mlsbench` 列出它们。
140 题里 `gpus = 0` 的有 24 个，去掉要调外部 LLM API 的 `agent-tool-reasoning` 和 `mas-topology`，剩 22 个。

**没有正式批次**：它是阶段三做实验岗位（experiment）的训练环境（#141、#157），题目由 #157 选定；`src/tasks/batches/mlsbench.yaml` 是全集，不在 `plan.batches` 里。
资源：每题 8 CPU、32 GB（`ml-active-learning` 64 GB）；官方 agent 时限 5 小时；验证在同一个任务容器里运行，时间从几十秒到几小时不等。

## 怎么运行和评分

- 官方入口：Harbor 包让任何 Harbor agent 在任务环境里运行（`harbor run -c run.yaml --path tasks-docker/mls-bench__<任务> --agent <agent>`）；评分是 Harbor 的验证器 `tests/test.sh`，没有 LLM（来源：MANIFEST.yaml `run`）。
- 验证器：编辑范围守卫（对比 `tests/meta/pristine`，改范围外的行或新建文件算无效，reward 为 0）→ 运行任务的全部评测脚本（含隐藏设置）→ 解析指标，按 `score_spec` 对基线归一化聚合成 `combined_score`，限制到 [0, 1] 写成 `reward.txt`。

## 一道题：交给系统什么、怎么评分（Issue #161）

写作 `mlsbench/<任务>`，coding-agent 和 ResearchWorld 都可以运行：

```bash
uv run researchworld_eval run coding-agent mlsbench/ml-anomaly-detection --condition CC-sonnet --purpose smoke
uv run researchworld_eval score mlsbench-verifier <run-id>
```

- **给系统的（候选侧，`researchworld_eval.benchmarks.mlsbench` 渲染）**：任务的环境镜像（`rwe-bench-mls-env:<任务>-<哈希>`，基础镜像按 digest 固定，`/workspace` 里是 scaffold）；提示是 `instruction.md` 原文；
  能在镜像里工作的系统（coding-agent、ResearchWorld）就在镜像里，其余系统得到从镜像拷出的 `/workspace`（别名 `/workspace`）。
- **不给的**：`tests/`（评测脚本、隐藏设置、解析器、score spec、基线榜单、pristine 树）和 `solution/`（oracle）；它们只在验证时由 Harbor 挂载。框架拒绝含这些名字的候选侧。
- **交付物**：任务声明的可编辑文件（`tests/meta/config.json` 的 `files[].filename`，如 `/workspace/scikit-learn/custom_anomaly.py`）。
- **时间上限**：照官方 5 小时（`task.toml`），连同 CPU 和内存作为题目的条件；一周统一上限之内。
- **联网屏蔽**：`task.toml` 写着 `allow_internet = true`，但基础镜像带着数据，所以按离线题，只放行包索引（共同问题 C4）。屏蔽表（[`shield.yaml`](shield.yaml)）挡 benchmark 自己的材料：
  仓库、任务数据集、论文、榜单站点和 Docker Hub 上的任务镜像；MLS-Bench 的任务不是由某一篇论文派生的，没有逐题的原论文；日期上限取仓库创建日 2026-05-08。
- **评分**：评测系统 [`mlsbench-verifier`](../../../evaluators/mlsbench_verifier/README.md)，主分数 `metrics.reward`（0–1）。

### 与官方协议的差异

- 官方 Harbor 在 agent 运行后直接验证整个 `/workspace`；这里只把交付的可编辑文件上传给验证器。范围外的改动和新建文件不会被守卫看到（比官方宽松），范围内的改动与官方一致。
- 基础镜像按 digest 固定，不是 `latest`。
- 网络只放行包索引。
- 本机 Harbor 是 0.20.0（作者在 0.6.6 和 0.22.0 上测过）；`schema_version = "1.1"` 的任务包在 0.20.0 上能解析和运行（冒烟里验证）。

## 公开对照分数

读取日 2026-11-01，[榜单](https://mls-bench.com/leaderboard)页面内嵌的 MLS-Bench Lite（30 题）总分，人类 SOTA 44.66：

| 模型 | 配置 | 总分 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Fable 5.1 | Claude Code（max effort） | 50.3 |
| GPT-6 Astra | Codex（max） | 50.0 |
| Claude Opus 5 | Claude Code（max effort） | 49.8 |
| Kimi K3 | Kimi-Code（max） | 48.3 |
| GPT 5.6 Sol | Codex（max） | 46.2 |
| Qwen3.8-Max | Claude Code | 41.0 |
| Claude Sonnet 5 | Claude Code（max effort） | 31.4 |

（来源：MANIFEST.yaml `published_scores`。榜单只有 30 题 Lite 的总分，其中多数要 GPU；没有逐题分数，也没有 22 个 CPU 题的单独汇总，所以不登记为 #127 的逐题 baseline。）

## 冒烟（Issue #161）

同一道题 `mlsbench/ml-anomaly-detection`（无监督表格异常检测，scikit-learn 基础镜像，4 个评测设置），两个系统各一次，`--purpose smoke`，**时限 1 小时**（官方 5 小时；冒烟只证明接入走通，所以用 `--hours 1` 压低预算），评分 `mlsbench-verifier`（Harbor 0.20.0，无 LLM）：

| 系统 | 运行 | 墙钟 | 花费（按价目表折算，订阅无实收） | reward |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CC-sonnet（coding-agent，Claude Code + `claude-sonnet-5-5`，high） | `coding-agent-mlsbench--ml-anomaly-detection-20261101T195313Z` | 155 s | $0.165 | 0.328 |
| RW-sonnet（ResearchWorld，HuTian 4.2.0，`claude-sonnet-5-5`，high） | `researchworld-mlsbench--ml-anomaly-detection-20261101T195313Z` | 2940 s | $3.127 | 0.343 |

两次评分都跑完 4 个评测设置（cardio、thyroid、satellite、shuttle），没有评测失败和编辑范围违规；验证约 77 秒。只证明接入走通，不比较系统：一题一次。

notes.model: claude-sonnet-5-5 through the Anthropic Messages API (llm.provider=anthropic), no fallback models, reviewer model = same model. Requests carry model, messages and max_tokens only (no tools); thinking: {'type': 'between_tools'} is sent, which turns thinking off; ARC's per-stage temperature is not sent because the model rejects it, so the API default applies.
notes.agent: ARC is not a tool-using coding agent: its 23-stage pipeline, its own code agent and its reviewers are prompt chains over plain chat completions. conditions.agent=claude means only that the provider is Anthropic; Claude Code is not involved. E2E tasks run ARC's own docker mode (experiment.mode=docker, docker.network_policy=setup_only, #220): every generated experiment runs in a fresh container of the experiment image (the same CPU Python stack as ARC's image, started by ARC through the host docker socket, on the run's shield network, with the condition's cpus and memory). ARC's entrypoint there installs requirements.txt, runs the generated setup.py (network through the shield: the task's data is downloaded here, into /workspace/data), cuts the network (iptables) and only then runs main.py. A benchmark item keeps experiment.mode=sandbox (a plain subprocess in ARC's container, no network from the experiment's point of view: ARC's code-generation prompt for that mode forbids external data).
notes.experiment: E2E tasks run ARC's own docker mode (experiment.mode=docker, docker.network_policy=setup_only, #220): every generated experiment runs in a fresh container of the experiment image (the same CPU Python stack as ARC's image, started by ARC through the host docker socket, on the run's shield network, with the condition's cpus and memory). A benchmark item keeps experiment.mode=sandbox (a plain subprocess in ARC's container, no network from the experiment's point of view: ARC's code-generation prompt for that mode forbids external data).
notes.effort: ARC has no effort setting; usage-log.patch sends output_config.effort='high' with every request. Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 think by default and ARC's per-stage max_tokens (4096, 8192, 16384) is shared with the thinking tokens: at high effort a stage can end with thinking only and no text (#106). notes.venue: Not chosen by the system: export.target_conference=iclr_2026 comes from [systems.autoresearchclaw].
notes.tokens: ARC records no usage. A logging-only patch (usage-log.patch) appends each Messages API `usage` block to anthropic-usage.jsonl; cost is not computed. The same patch carries the RWE_OMIT_TEMPERATURE, RWE_EFFORT and RWE_THINKING switches.
notes.time: No global wall-clock or budget cap in ARC; only the runner's limit applies. Per experiment run 3600 s (in docker mode ARC passes it as the timeout of the whole container: pip install, setup.py and main.py), refinement iterations 10, repair cycles 3.
notes.input: Chinese pack text goes verbatim (candidate files concatenated, with <!-- file --> markers) into prompts.extra_prompts of 18 stages. ARC takes one topic string and checks generated code against it, so research.topic is the candidate TASK.md with whitespace collapsed, in its faithful English version (candidate/TASK.en.md) when the task has one (#196: the keywords ARC's literature screen filters by are taken from the ASCII words of the topic, and a Chinese topic leaves only the file names it mentions); the run's result says which text it was (notes.topic_source). Literature queries come from the stage-3 model plan; ARC's ASCII keyword splitter and its whitespace-based query expansion yield a few useless queries from the Chinese text. Starter papers are guidance text only: ARC cannot ingest seed papers.

conditions.notes_en: Added by the maintainer on 2026-11-02 (#185): the GPT-6.1 Sol column of phase 1. ARC uses its own OpenAI-compatible client (llm.provider=openai-compatible, wire_api=responses) through codex-api on `codex-2`; ARC has no effort setting, so openai-route.patch puts reasoning.effort on every request (as the output_config.effort patch does for the Anthropic route; apart from read-only logging the only change). ARC's per-stage max_tokens cannot be eaten by thinking on this route (the problem of #106): the max_output_tokens and temperature ARC sends are removed by codex-api before the request reaches Codex, so the problem of #106 does not exist on this route. Effort is medium, unlike the high of the other conditions (maintainer, 2026-11-04, #227): on the ChatGPT-subscription (Codex login) route OpenAI's backend resets a single request's stream at about 900 s (codex-api answers 500, #223); ARC stage 10 generates all the experiment code in one request, which at high often runs past 15 minutes, and after the cut ARC retries the same request into the same limit. Lowering the effort is a request parameter that sets the experiment condition (precedent: ARC-opus, #106); ARC's prompts, stages and algorithm are untouched.

notes.tokens: ARC records no usage. openai-route.patch appends each response's `usage` block and the request seconds to anthropic-usage.jsonl (the same log as the Messages API route); cost is not computed, there is no per-token charge on a ChatGPT plan.
notes.time: No global wall-clock or budget cap in ARC; only the runner's limit applies. Per experiment run 3600 s (in docker mode ARC passes it as the timeout of the whole container: pip install, setup.py and main.py), refinement iterations 10, repair cycles 3.
notes.input: Chinese pack text goes verbatim (candidate files concatenated, with <!-- file --> markers) into prompts.extra_prompts of 18 stages. ARC takes one topic string and checks generated code against it, so research.topic is the candidate TASK.md with whitespace collapsed, in its faithful English version (candidate/TASK.en.md) when the task has one (#196: the keywords ARC's literature screen filters by are taken from the ASCII words of the topic, and a Chinese topic leaves only the file names it mentions); the run's result says which text it was (notes.topic_source). Literature queries come from the stage-3 model plan; ARC's ASCII keyword splitter and its whitespace-based query expansion yield a few useless queries from the Chinese text. Starter papers are guidance text only: ARC cannot ingest seed papers.
notes.search: Web search, crawling, GitHub, HF Hub, Gemini and OpenCode are off. Literature search in stage 4 uses ['openalex', 'semantic_scholar'] through ARC's own clients behind the shield proxy; stages 8, 17, 22 and 23 (novelty, citation verification) always also query arXiv, CrossRef and DataCite; the shield date-bounds those API calls like the others (a late DOI answers 403).
notes.server_side_search: Not reachable: every request is built in researchclaw/llm/client.py and carries only model, input, max_output_tokens, temperature and reasoning, never a tools or web_search field; web_search.enabled=false. The only host address the shield lets through is codex-api's model routes.
notes.secrets: An E2E task's experiments run in containers that get none of ARC's environment (only the shield's proxy variables and CA bundle). A benchmark item's experiment code runs as a subprocess and inherits the container environment: a placeholder key only (the shield proxy puts codex-api's local key on the request).
notes.profile: project.profile=ml_generic is fixed for all tasks; research.domains is left empty because the literature screen rejects papers outside the stated domain (a theory task failed with domains=[machine-learning]).

meaning.en: AutoResearchClaw; provider openai, reasoning effort medium.

notes.server_side_search: Not reachable: EvoScientist binds no provider-side search tool to any model (its only tools are think_tool, tavily_search when TAVILY_API_KEY is set, MCP tools from mcp.yaml, deepagents built-ins and skills; EvoScientist/EvoScientist.py:671-672 and 754-755 at the pin; the one bind_tools call is the tool selector's own output schema, middleware/tool_selector.py:166). TAVILY_API_KEY is not passed and the image has no mcp.yaml, so no search tool exists. Anthropic/OpenAI hosts are only tunnelled by the shield, so a provider-side search would be invisible to the audit.
notes.credentials: The provider key is in the process environment and EvoScientist's execute shell inherits the environment (upstream has no switch); the key is therefore visible to the agent's shell. It is a run-scoped copy and is not logged by this adapter.
notes.memory: A fresh data dir per run (baked skills, empty memory). Memory workers, skill synthesis and the scheduler stay at upstream defaults, so their LLM calls count in the usage log.
notes.limits: async sub-agents off (README advice for scripted runs); recursion_limit=1000000; model retry wait in auto-mode 1800 s (time without progress counts as wall time); execute timeout 300 s per command. No token or cost budget exists.
